Method of Attack: Using fake error logs storing ASCII characters disguised as hexadecimal values that decode to a malicious payload
Scheduled task impersonating a legitimate one with a similar name and description
Renamed copies of legitimate executables (mshta.exe and powershell.exe) to appear innocuous
Execution of VBScript to start PowerShell and run commands
Extraction and decoding of ASCII numbers from fake log to obtain payload
In-memory patch to Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) to bypass script-based attack detection
Downloader command retrieving additional PowerShell commands
Payload gathering system reconnaissance information including installed browsers, tax-preparation, security products, and point-of-sale software
Discoverer: John Ferrell, VP of ThreatOps at Huntress Labs
Impacted Systems: Systems with security products (Kaspersky, Comodo, Defender)
Indicators of Compromise: File named 'a.chk' containing fake error log with hexadecimal values
Scheduled task with name similar to legitimate task
Executables named 'BfeOnService.exe' and 'engine.exe' as renamed copies of mshta.exe and powershell.exe
Attack Vector: File masquerading as Windows error log
Execution of PowerShell commands via renamed executables
